- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00), model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply a downward bias of 1–3% per sentiment drop.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for downside risk.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence in short-term momentum; if recent 7-day trend is upward, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid “overfitting” to recent gains.
